From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). 11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Buyer Review of Seller SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

## Preliminary point: the "[STANDARD]" labels and the "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package marks most clauses "[STANDARD]" and says they are "reviewed and cleared by both sides." It also says the Buyer has "already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package." **Nothing in the material shows any agreement to this.** These are labels the Seller applied to its own draft. I have reviewed every item on its merits, and I recommend you reject in writing the suggestion that any point is agreed.

Two further points apply throughout:
- **The data room is stale.** It is fixed at 5.00pm on 22 September 2026, and today is 5 November 2026.
- **The Seller's own Disclosure Letter contradicts its SPA cover note** on Bluefen, Riverlark, the bonuses and the incident.

---

**SPA-N-001: General liability cap**
- **Seller:** 20% of price (AUD 4.8m) for general Warranty Claims.
- **Buyer wants:** 20–30% for general warranties only. Fundamental warranties, tax and specific indemnities should sit outside this cap.
- **Recommendation:** Accept 20% only if it is confined to general warranties and backed by W&I cover. Otherwise counter at 30%. *Reason: 20% is within market for general warranties, but not when it is applied to every claim (see N-014).*

**SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket**
- **Seller:** AUD 25k de minimis. AUD 250k basket (about 1.04%), operating as a deductible so only the excess is recoverable.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis of about AUD 20–25k. A tipping basket of about 0.5% (AUD 120k), so that once it is exceeded the claim is recoverable from the first dollar. Related claims should aggregate for the de minimis.
- **Recommendation:** Accept the de minimis with related-claims aggregation. Counter with a tipping basket of AUD 120k. *Reason: a deductible above 1% shifts too much first-loss risk onto the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-003: General claims time limit**
- **Seller:** 18 months, and "any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated."
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months, or at least two full audit cycles, for general warranties. Separate, longer periods for title/capacity, tax and the specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** Counter at 24 months and reverse the default. *Reason: an 18-month all-claims default would wipe out tax and indemnity protection.*

**SPA-N-004: Fundamental and title regime**
- **Seller:** Title and capacity warranties get the same cap and time limit as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer wants:** A cap of 100% of the price (AUD 24m). A time limit of at least 6–7 years. No de minimis or basket. Not qualified by disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: if title fails, the Buyer has bought nothing, and a 20% cap would leave 80% of the price unprotected.*

**SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out**
- **Seller:** No carve-out. Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3, 12.8, 20.5) apply "to all Claims of any nature."
- **Buyer wants:** An express carve-out from every limitation, the exclusive remedy, non-reliance and the knowledge qualifier. It should cover fraud, dishonesty and wilful concealment by the Seller, the Company, and their officers, employees and advisers.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and insert the carve-out. *Reason: this is non-negotiable market practice, and NSW law disfavours exclusions of liability for fraud, so silence invites dispute.*

**SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope**
- **Seller:** General disclosure of the whole data room, the Accounts, the statutory registers and public records (DL 1.1–1.2). Clause 1.4 says nothing admits materiality.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific disclosures only, made fairly and with enough detail for the Buyer to assess the nature and scope of the matter. General disclosure limited to named searches at named dates. No disclosure against fundamental or tax warranties, or the specific indemnities. Any update against warranties repeated at Completion should give the Buyer a termination right, not cure the breach.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the general data-room disclosure and require a "fair disclosure" standard. *Reason: blanket data-room disclosure guts the warranties, and this data room is now six weeks old.*

**SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier**
- **Seller:** No claim for anything the Buyer or its advisers knew, or that was "discoverable" from the data room or public records (cl 8.3).
- **Buyer wants:** An express statement that Buyer knowledge does not bar or reduce claims (pro-sandbagging). At minimum, limit the bar to the actual knowledge of named deal-team individuals of matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: imputed and "discoverable" knowledge, together with general disclosure, would exclude almost every claim.*

**SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent**
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours. The condition is treated as satisfied on delivery of a written consent. DL item 2 admits there is no final consent and no evidence the cl 11.3 conditions are met.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A condition precedent, waivable only by the Buyer, requiring an unconditional written consent (or one on terms acceptable to the Buyer) and evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
  - All reasonable endeavours by the Seller.
  - A long-stop termination right.
  - A specific indemnity for loss of the contract or revenue if consent is later challenged.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the "satisfied on delivery" drafting. *Reason: Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m, roughly 30% of FY26 revenue, and is central to value.*

**SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility**
- **Seller:** Release "to be provided following Completion." DL item 3 confirms the facility is unpaid and no discharge exists.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Treat the facility (about AUD 3.2m plus break costs and interest) as Debt, deducted from the price.
  - Pay it directly to Riverlark through the funds flow at Completion.
  - As completion deliverables: a payout letter, deeds of release, PPSR discharge, and release of any share security.
  - Address the change-control right in cl 8.1.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-Completion release. *Reason: on a debt-free basis, the Buyer must not take the Company subject to AUD 3.2m of debt or security, including any security over the shares being bought.*

**SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses**
- **Seller:** "A matter for the Seller," and not in the funds flow. DL item 5 confirms AUD 420k is omitted and payroll tax and superannuation are unaddressed.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Treat AUD 420k plus all on-costs (payroll tax, superannuation, PAYG, workers' compensation) as Transaction Costs or Debt, deducted from the price.
  - Pay through Company payroll at Completion.
  - A specific indemnity, with leakage protection.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: the Company is the employer, so without these steps the Buyer funds roughly AUD 450k+ on top of the agreed price.*

**SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity**
- **Seller:** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment. DL item 4 records AUD 180k open, with no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A broad specific indemnity covering any loss from the Company not owning, or Ironquay asserting rights over, the SOW3 Project Materials. This should include claims, remediation and re-development costs.
  - The indemnity should sit outside the general cap and basket, with its own longer time limit.
  - As a completion deliverable: evidence of cleared payment, or payment from the Seller's proceeds, plus a confirmatory IP assignment.
- **Recommendation:** Reject as inadequate. *Reason: under cl 7.3, IP passes only on payment, so the exposure is the IP itself, not AUD 180k.*

**SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident**
- **Seller:** "Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material." DL item 6 says up to about 1,240 records may be affected, access is unknown, and scope and notification status are unresolved.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Before Completion: an independent forensic report and the Privacy Act eligible-data-breach assessment. The 30-day assessment window has likely passed if the incident predates 22 September.
  - A specific indemnity, outside the general cap and basket, covering notification and response costs, OAIC action and penalties (to the extent lawful), third-party claims and customer losses.
  - Warranties of no other incidents and of NDB compliance.
  - Conduct rights over the response.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the characterisation. *Reason: the regulatory and contractual exposure is unquantified, and the Seller's own disclosure does not support "not material."*

**SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals**
- **Seller:** AUD 330k (3 × 110k) of "ordinary-course operating costs." DL item 8 does not say whether the renewals are committed, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Disclosure of the terms, dates and related-party status. DL item 8 says "related," so this needs clarifying.
  - A pre-Completion conduct covenant that bars further renewals without Buyer consent.
  - Unaccrued committed amounts not in the ordinary course to be treated as Debt or leakage, or covered by a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Do not accept as ordinary course until verified. *Reason: AUD 330k of linked renewals in the sale window looks like a commitment loaded onto the Buyer.*

**SPA-N-014: Category separation**
- **Seller:** A single limitation regime applies to "all Claims of any nature" unless expressly stated otherwise. Title, tax and IP are folded into the general regime.
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regimes, each with its own cap and time limit:
  - general warranties
  - fundamental warranties
  - tax warranties and the tax indemnity
  - specific indemnities (Ironquay, privacy, bonuses, Riverlark, Bluefen)
  - price adjustment and leakage
  
  Specific indemnities should be excluded from the de minimis, basket and disclosure, and the default should be reversed.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. *Reason: merging the categories is the mechanism that turns every other concession into a 20% cap with an 18-month limit.*

**SPA-N-015: Title verification**
- **Seller:** Relies on the share register at DD-012. DL item 10 concedes the Buyer has not verified title.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - Current ASIC company extract and share-structure search.
  - Original share certificates, or a lost-certificate indemnity.
  - Issue and transfer history, plus any options, convertibles or rights.
  - PPSR search on the Seller and the Company, with a release of any Riverlark security over the shares.
  - Signed transfers at Completion.
  - A fundamental title warranty under the N-004 regime.
- **Recommendation:** Do not rely on the register alone. *Reason: the register proves what is recorded, not that the shares are unencumbered and fully paid.*

**SPA-N-016: Tax and IP open terms**
- **Seller:** "Settled under the general regime." The Buyer has agreed no such thing.
- **Buyer wants:**
  - A standalone tax indemnity for pre-Completion tax.
  - A cap of 100% of price and a time limit of the ATO amendment period plus about 6 months (in practice 5–7 years), unlimited for fraud or evasion.
  - Payroll tax, superannuation guarantee and GST expressly covered.
  - IP warranties raised to near-fundamental status (higher cap, longer period), given Ironquay.
- **Recommendation:** Treat as OPEN and table the Buyer's tax deed and IP terms. *Reason: an 18-month, 20%-capped tax remedy would expire before most ATO audits begin.*

---

## Also flag (not on your list)
- **DD-007 lease and DD-009 Mossvale:** Seller-favourable characterisations. Confirm whether the lease notice and Mossvale assignment provisions are actually triggered by a change of control. If they are, make the notice a completion deliverable.
- **Refresh:** Require an updated data room and a bring-down Disclosure Letter. Make any new adverse matter a termination trigger, not an automatic disclosure.

**Suggested next step:** Send the Buyer's mark-up with a covering note stating that no clause is agreed. Lead with N-014, N-005, N-004, N-009 and N-010, because these carry the largest value at risk.
